source: AGR-XWALK-011 South African statutory clause architecture validation

authorities_validated: National Credit Act 34 of 2005 sections 4 and 6 and related applicable provisions
Companies Act 71 of 2008 sections 44, 45 and 50-53 plus takeover provisions
Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 section 45(2A) amendment effective 27 December 2024
Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002 sections 11-14
Financial Intelligence Centre Act Schedule 1 Item 11
Securities Transfer Tax Act 25 of 2007 and Administration Act 26 of 2007
Competition Act 89 of 1998 and Competition Commission merger thresholds effective 1 May 2026
material_findings: NCA applicability must be classified; a bilateral corporate facility is not automatically subject to the full NCA clause regime.
FIC Item 11 can cover credit-provider business even where certain credit agreements are excluded from NCA application.
Companies Act sections 44 and 45 require separate applicability tests; section 45(2A) excludes financial assistance to or for the benefit of subsidiaries from section 45.
A certificated securities transfer requires a proper instrument of transfer or operation of law before securities-register entry.
STT applies to listed and unlisted securities at the current 0.25% rate subject to statutory exemptions and has specific unlisted-transfer notification/payment timing.
SPA promotion requires a current Competition Act merger-control test; thresholds changed effective 1 May 2026.
Electronic execution requires an ECTA formality check rather than a blanket e-signature assumption.
controlled_gaps: No operative South African clause wording has yet been approved for any of the three templates.
Collateral-specific common-law pledge, cession, perfection and enforcement validation remains outstanding.
No controlled transaction instance has yet bound the statutory applicability facts and corporate records to the templates.
